title: Our House: Day Versus Night
trend: TikTok + Instagram Reels Halloween 'Decor: Day vs. Night' (same decorated house shown in daylight, then after dark; New Engen 2026 Halloween TikTok & Reels list) + final week before Halloween (Oct 31)
length_reason: Quick one-clip before-and-after format (the originals run well under a minute), so it stays at the short end; 180 s keeps it eligible for TikTok and Instagram too.
youtube_title: Our House: Day Versus Night (Dad Went Too Far for Halloween)
description:
Bree wants to show the whole block their house by day and by night before Halloween. By day: cozy mums and a dad with a mug. By night: fog, screaming and nine floodlights.
The light timer has been keeping a secret, and the fox on the lawn is not a statue.

lines.text: Our house, day versus night. Let's start with day.
Good morning, neighbors. Fresh mums. Warm cider. A dad with a mug.
And now, night.
Who dares walk upon my lawn!
Same man. Same mug. Different energy.
The cape makes me taller. It's science.
Okay, the pumpkins. By day, they are smiling.
Friendly. Approachable. Good with kids.
By night, Dad turns them all around.
I carved an angry face on the back. Two faced pumpkins.
Twice the carving. Twice the seeds.
We are eating pumpkin seeds until March.
Now, the lights. That's the timer's job.
Good evening. I decide when it is night.
It's eleven in the morning.
That is your opinion.
The fog machine went off at noon yesterday.
The mail lady walked into the fog and came out a different person.
She now throws the mail from the sidewalk.
A bill hit me in the forehead.
And by day, we have a cute little fox statue.
Nineteen dollars at the garden store. Very lifelike.
Evening.
The statue said evening.
I'm not a statue. I stand still professionally.
Dad, where did you get the statue?
From the lawn. He was already here. I assumed it came with the house.
I did come with the house. I'm in the paperwork.
So who ate the candy bowl last night?
Your sign said take one. I am one fox.
That's fair. I hate that it's fair.
Okay, final night shot. Timer, make it dark.
I cannot.
What do you mean you cannot?
He has nine floodlights. Night never happens here.
The birds think it's spring. The rooster next door crows at midnight.
Dad. Why do we have nine floodlights?
For safety. For the decorations. For the art.
He made me promise. The dark never comes.
Dad. Are you afraid of the dark?
I am not afraid of the dark.
I'm afraid of what's in the dark. Which is the dark.
You built a haunted house!
A very bright haunted house. With a night light in every coffin.
The skeleton has a reading lamp. He's halfway through a mystery.
So our night version is brighter than our day version.
From space, this porch is the sun.
I just wanted the kids to see where the candy is.
I can see where the candy is.
Timer, please. One real night shot.
Very well. I quit. Good night.
Bree. Bree. Why is it dark.
This is what night looks like, Dad.
Everyone does this every night?
Finally. Now this is a haunted house.
Our house. Day versus night.
Day. Day forever. Somebody turn the day back on.
